goal_outcomes.goal1: Replaced by goal2 before a finish flag; do not call completed.
goal_outcomes.finish_boundary: One finish=true in bag, after goal2. Nearest odometry is offset from flag and nonzero velocity; finish does not mean exact centre or certified physical rest.

initial_motion.zero_definition: Both published cmd_vel.linear.x and angular.z absolute <=1e-6; command pulses do not alone measure wheel stop.
initial_motion.conclusion: Intermittent zero output already occurs about 16s before the first slow ABORT and about 112s before first optional MPPI refresh. Later collision recovery and optional solves cannot explain the beginning of this symptom. See mppi_navigation_audit.json for input age/cycle rejection causes.

fault_log.message: [FSM] Tracker reported excessive trajectory error; abort old trajectory and replan from odometry.

first_abort.causal_evidence: MPPI capture has no active snapshot after a delta/cache decode exception. reject(reason) publishes zero and, for an active goal that already received commands, raises tracking_fault because this raw decoder reason is absent from LOCAL_RETRY_REJECTIONS. FSM consumes the Boolean and logs the generic excessive-error text, then EMERGENCY_STOP publishes ABORT. The generic FSM text is not evidence that a measured tracking-error threshold caused this episode.
first_abort.ordering_boundary: reject publishes fault before log/status. Fault receipt before the MPPI warning/status is consistent with this source order; cross-topic stamps cannot alone reverse the cause.
first_abort.cache_protocol_boundary: Independent observer received a new full before its deltas, and controller last successful adoption remained previous full. The exact failed incoming sequence is not logged; queue drop/scheduling is consistent, not directly proven.

raw_live_collision.meaning: collision_is_dynamic here includes latest live LiDAR occupancy. It does not require a moving cluster or intentional human crossing. The warning label dynamic obstacle is not a classification witness.
raw_live_collision.geometry_findings: All 19 selected stop voxels have actual same-window mapping points. Twelve points are suspiciously fixed in source-stamp body coordinates x=.188-.202m, y=-.024..+.013m, z=.194-.208m; physical fixed-sphere gaps10.04-13.85mm lie just outside 10mm self-filter padding, while planner clearance includes a50mm voxel margin. Other seven have body x~.37-.43m.
raw_live_collision.geometry_boundary: Fresh near-field input and inconsistent filtering/planning margins are confirmed; physical identity of returns is not. AABB/sphere proximity/body-coordinate clustering do not prove a particular robot shell surface. Extrinsic error, near-field multipath, selection bias at filter boundary, and nearby external objects are not independently excluded. These later19 stops do not explain earliest zero pulses.

optional_refresh.conclusion: Five actual optional attempts, two successes. Production live event contains no MPPI prefix. The first attempt begins around20:04:35.688 after initial stutter/firstABORT. tryMppiRefresh failure restores old guide metadata and does not itself publish ABORT.

overlapping_second_fault.boundary: Fault arrived during synchronous optional solve and was processed after it. This proves fault/ABORT path, not that optional solve caused the geometry failure or that CPU contention had no role.

yaw_continuity_boundary.interpretation: Matching/fresh progress does not prove the physical robot aligns with the future guide heading. This witness needs separate handoff acceptance/actuation analysis; do not attribute its cause solely from these stamps.

phase_clock_witness.interpretation: At first live collision, scan used controller phase rather than90s wallclock fallback; this historical bug is not reproduced at this witness.

prior_fix_checks.transient_recovery: 19 recovery completions and no goal-giveup. Recovery fix operates, but recovering from repeatedly flagged near-field points can still create repeated stops.
prior_fix_checks.ordinary_static_urgent_one_line_route: Not exercised: no ordinary Emergency stop! witness; helper behavior cannot be claimed real-vehicle accepted for an unobserved entrance.

limits: No dynamic crossing was deliberately performed; user reported open transfer. Dynamic output presence/absence cannot independently prove physical human entry time.
This core audit does not identify physical objects from live points; use separate source-stamp cloud/TF evidence with its limitations.
Zero cmd/trajectory ABORT are explicit software events, not exact physical-stop onset.
No source/parameter changes or simulation were made in this audit.
